# lr-fsmap test fixtures

Captured tool output used to pin the `dumpe2fs` and `xfs_db` parsers. These are
samples, not regenerated by tests, so the parsers are checked against output
that a real filesystem actually produced.

## Provenance

| File | Produced by |
|---|---|
| `ext4-fresh.dumpe2fs.txt` | `truncate -s 256M ext4.img && mkfs.ext4 -F -q -L ROOTFS ext4.img && dumpe2fs ext4.img` |
| `ext4-fragmented.dumpe2fs.txt` | Same 256 MiB image, then 400 files of random 4 KiB–40 KiB written with `debugfs -w -f cmds.txt`, then every second file removed (`rm /f<i>`) so the free list contains 202 extents |
| `xfs-fresh.sb.txt` | `truncate -s 512M xfs.img && mkfs.xfs -f -q -L XFSROOT xfs.img && xfs_db -r -c "sb 0" -c "print blocksize" -c "print agblocks" -c "print agcount" -c "print dblocks" -c "print logstart" -c "print rblocks" xfs.img` |
| `xfs-fresh.freesp.txt` | `xfs_db -r -c "freesp -d" -c "freesp -s" xfs.img` |

`xfs_db` was 6.6.0 and `dumpe2fs` came from e2fsprogs 1.47 (Ubuntu 24.04).

## Expected parse results

Computed independently in Python from the fixtures themselves, and cross-checked
against the totals the tools print (`Free blocks:` in the superblock section,
`total free extents`/`total free blocks` at the end of `freesp -s`). The tests
pin exactly these numbers.

| Fixture | Expected |
|---|---|
| `ext4-fresh` | block size 4096, block count 65536, first block 0, free blocks 57268, 2 free ranges, **2 used extents, 33865728 used bytes** |
| `ext4-fragmented` | free blocks 56046, 202 free ranges, **202 used extents, 38871040 used bytes** |
| `xfs-fresh` | block size 4096, agblocks 32768, agcount 4, dblocks 131072, logstart 65543, rblocks 0, 29 free extents / 114652 free blocks, **5 used extents, 67256320 used bytes** |

## Format notes that matter to the parser

* `dumpe2fs` prints one `Free blocks:` line per group, indented by two spaces,
  and the superblock-level `Free blocks:` total at column zero. A group with no
  free blocks still gets the indented line, with an empty range list.
* `print_free()` in e2fsprogs does not truncate the list, so the ranges are
  complete; the parser still cross-checks their sum against the superblock total
  and fails loudly if they disagree.
* `xfs_db -c "freesp -d"` ends with a histogram whose rows have five columns;
  `freesp -s` appends `total free extents`/`total free blocks` lines at column
  zero. Only lines with exactly three integers are extents.
* An XFS filesystem with an external log reports `logstart = 0`; one with a
  realtime device reports `rblocks > 0`. Both make the used-block map
  incomplete by design (`complete = false`).
